scope: Dimension-uniform representation, pair-star, pure-seed support and comparator-separation reduction for complex Spin(2n+1) spinors; the all-n mixed-star bound remains unresolved.

costs.new_computation: No new exact star extraction, SDP, numerical optimization, or finitecompiler was run or created.
costs.analytic_derivations: Closed Clifford-word counts, gamma-trace branching, and finite-dimensional convex separation; no data acquisition cost.
costs.orbit_channels: Haar Spin-orbit POVMs are existence constructions; finite-outcome discretization and implementation costs are not supplied.
costs.inherited_exact_checks: Cycle 9: 4096-dimensional triple product reduced to nine blocks and ten support rays. Cycle 10: 32768-dimensional triple product reduced to 11 blocks; 17 seed-support rays and 629 exact principal minors.

claims.statement: For the complex spinor S of Spin(2n+1), dim(S)=d=2^n and End(S)=direct_sum_{k=0}^n Lambda^k R^(2n+1). The full triple product S* tensor S tensor S decomposes as direct_sum_{r=0}^n T_r tensor C^(n+1-r), with highest weight (3/2 repeated r, 1/2 repeated n-r) and dim(T_r)=d(C(2n+1,r)-C(2n+1,r-1)). The output-swap multiplicities are m_{r,±}=#{j=r,...,n : (-1)^((n-j)(n-j+1)/2)=±1}.
assumptions: The standard complex irreducible Clifford module for Spin(2n+1), with odd Clifford volume acting as a scalar.
The gamma-trace map on spinor-valued j-forms has the standard surjective recursion for 0<=j<=n.
The invariant bilinear-form symmetry convention gives flip sign (-1)^((n-j)(n-j+1)/2) on Lambda^j in S tensor S.
claims.falsifier: A failure of the gamma-trace branching, a mismatch in a highest weight or flip sign, or failure of the dimension identity falsifies the claim.

claims.statement: For Clifford grade k and pair grade j, K_k=sum_|A|=k T_A^T tensor T_A has eigenvalue mu_(k,j)=sum_{ell=0}^{min(k,j)} (-1)^(kj-ell) C(j,ell) C(2n+1-j,k-ell). In the 12-coupling basis of each triple multiplicity space M_r, the full star block is H_(alpha,r)=sum_k alpha_k(D_(k,r)+F_r D_(k,r) F_r), where D_(k,r)=diag(mu_(k,r),...,mu_(k,n)) and F_r is the output-swap orthogonal involution. Both swap eigenspaces and every grade k=1,...,n are retained.
assumptions: Hermitian Clifford generators square to identity and anticommute pairwise.
The Choi vectorization is |X>>=(I tensor X)|Omega>>.
The decomposition and multiplicity basis in C11-SPINOR-GRADE-AND-TRIPLE-DECOMPOSITION are used.
claims.falsifier: An incorrect Clifford commutation sign, a missing multiplicity copy, or an incomplete output-swap sector falsifies the reduction.

claims.statement: For nonnegative invariant weights alpha, support over all full-domain canonical measure-and-prepare channels equals h_n(alpha)=max over unit spinors psi of sum_k alpha_k s_k(psi), where s_k(psi)=sum_|A|=k |<psi,T_A psi>|^2. Each pure seed attains its score through its full-domain Spin-orbit POVM channel, whose transfer vector is eta_k=s_k/C(2n+1,k).
assumptions: Canonical measure-and-prepare prepares each normalized POVM effect state.
The Spin action on S is irreducible, so the Haar orbit rank-one POVM normalizes by Schur's lemma.
alpha_k>=0, so refining mixed POVM effects to pure effects cannot lower the quadratic support bound.
claims.scope_note: This identity does not classify the pure-spinor moment image or reduce its support to the listed seed family.

claims.statement: The Jordan-Wigner seed psi_0=|0^n> has moments s_k=C(n,floor(k/2)). For psi_h=(|0^n>+|1^h 0^(n-h)>)/sqrt(2), 1<=h<=n, the exact moments are the diagonal-plus-cross-word count in equation (7) of UNIFORM_REPRESENTATION_REPORT.md. At n=4 this reproduces (1,4,4,6), (0,1,7,7), (1,0,0,14); at n=5 it reproduces (1,5,5,10,10), (0,2,7,8,14), (1,1,1,14,14), (0,0,5,10,16).
assumptions: The five-qubit and four-qubit Jordan-Wigner Clifford convention from the cycle 9 and cycle 10 records is used, generalized to n qubits.
Binomial coefficients outside their range are zero.
claims.support_boundary: These are attained support witnesses and a lower bound on the full pure-state support; no all-n completeness claim is made.

claims.statement: For every pure spinor and n>=3, the Clifford grade moments obey s_k>=0, sum_(k=1)^n s_k=d-1, s_1<=1 and s_2<=n. Their support is bounded above by the support of O_n={s>=0: sum s_k=d-1, s_1<=1, s_2<=n}; the vertices of O_n have s_1 in {0,1}, s_2 in {0,n}, and all remaining mass on one grade j>=3. This outer bound is valid for signed weights alpha, but is not asserted tight for pure spinors.
assumptions: The Clifford grade basis is orthonormal under tau=Tr/d.
The grade-two Clifford image of a real 2-form in SO(2n+1) skew-normal form is a sum of n commuting Hermitian involutions.
claims.support_boundary: For nonnegative alpha the bound also upper-bounds canonical-EB support through C11-CANONICAL-EB-PURE-SUPPORT; for signed alpha it is stated only for pure-seed support.

claims.statement: Let W be any finite set of attained pure-seed moment vectors. If for all alpha>=0 the full ordinary-tensor star satisfies lambda_max(H_alpha)<=sum_k C(2n+1,k) alpha_k + max_(v in W) alpha dot v, then every Spin-covariant unital, trace-preserving, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint channel with a CPTP two-output extension having equal marginals admits one full-domain canonical EB comparator Psi with Psi-(2Phi-id)>=0 on Hermitian matrices. The criterion and separation step allow arbitrary real transfer vector lambda, including negative grade multipliers.
assumptions: The normalized Choi state is rho=J/d and the star convention is the one stated in the report.
The two-output broadcaster marginals equal Phi; symmetrization across outputs preserves this.
The displayed all-mixed star inequality holds for the selected seed set W.
claims.falsifier: A violation of the star inequality for an admitted alpha, or an error in normalized-Choi transfer identity or convex separation, invalidates the implication.

claims.statement: For every n>=1 and every alpha in R_+^n, lambda_max(H_alpha)<=sum_(k=1)^n C(2n+1,k) alpha_k + max_(0<=h<=n) sum_(k=1)^n alpha_k s_k(psi_h).
assumptions: All Clifford grades and both output-swap sectors are included.
The explicit all-n seed moments are those in equations (6)-(7).
